m: Meditation on Shri Chandika. Om. One should always remember her who shines like the bandhuka flower, who dwells upon five heads, whose jewelled crown flashes with the crescent moon, who wears a garland of heads, who is three-eyed, dressed in red, with full and high jar-like breasts, holding in order a book, a rosary, the boon, and the gesture of fearlessness, she who is honoured in the northern tradition. Or: may that Goddess, sovereign of the universe, protect me, she who is Chandi, crusher of the daityas beginning with Madhu and Kaitabha, uprooter of Mahisha, crusher of Dhumralochana, Chanda, and Munda, devourer of Raktabija, the power who crushes the daityas Shumbha and Nishumbha, the supreme giver of success, accompanied by nine crores of forms. Then the Argala hymn. Om. Of this Shri Argala hymn-mantra, the seer is Vishnu, the metre is anushtubh, and the deity is Shri Mahalakshmi. This direction is for its recitation as a limb of the Saptashati, to please the Mother of the world. Om. Salutation to Chandika. Markandeya said: Om. Victory to you, Goddess Chamunda. Victory, remover of the distress of beings. Victory, Goddess who go everywhere. Night of time, salutation to you.
Jayanti, Mangala, Kali, Bhadrakali, she of the skull, Durga, Shiva, forgiveness, the supporter, svaha, svadha: salutation to you.
Destroyer of Madhu and Kaitabha, giver of boons to the creator, salutation. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Destroyer of Mahishasura, giver of happiness to devotees, salutation. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Goddess, at the slaying of Dhumranetra, giver of dharma, desire, and wealth. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Goddess, at the slaying of Raktabija, destroyer of Chanda and Munda. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Destroyer of Nishumbha and Shumbha, giver of what is auspicious to the three worlds, salutation. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Goddess whose two feet are praised, giver of all good fortune. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
You whose form and deeds are beyond thought, destroyer of every enemy. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Aparna, remover of evil for those who always bow with devotion. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Chandika, destroyer of disease, for those who praise you with a devotion that comes first. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Chandika, always victorious in battle, destroyer of sin. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Give good fortune and health. Give, Goddess, the highest happiness. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Ordain welfare, Goddess. Ordain abundant prosperity. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Ordain the destruction of the hostile. Ordain strength in a high degree. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Ambika, whose feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of the heads of gods and asuras. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Make me possessed of learning, possessed of renown, and possessed of Lakshmi. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Goddess, queller of the pride of daityas by the fierce staff of your arm. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Chandika, slayer of the pride of fierce daityas, for me who have bowed. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Four-armed one, praised by the four-faced, supreme sovereign. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Goddess praised by Krishna, Ambika, always, with constant devotion. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Supreme sovereign, praised by the lord of the daughter of the snow mountain. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Supreme sovereign, worshipped with true feeling by the husband of Indrani. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Goddess, Ambika, in whom arises the joy given in abundance to devotees. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
Give a wife who delights the mind and who follows the course of the mind. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.
You who carry across the hard ocean of worldly life, born of the unmoving mountain. Give form. Give victory. Give renown. Slay the hostile.

Having recited this hymn, a person should recite the great hymn. Having fully worshipped the Saptashati, that person obtains a boon that is hard to obtain. Thus the Argala hymn in the Markandeya Purana is complete.
